dedupe_keys.name: future urban cycling demand in montreal under downscaled climate projections

description: This study by Xudong Wang, Eduardo Adame Valenzuela, Chenglong You, Van-Thanh-Van Nguyen, Lijun Sun and Luis Miranda-Moreno of McGill University (Transportation Research Part D, 2025) proposes a framework that combines weather-based cycling ridership models with downscaled climate projections to predict cycling demand under future climate scenarios. Coverage: Montreal, a cold-climate North American city, with projections to the 2050s under several scenarios. The city is expected to become warmer and drier, and ridership is projected to rise by 8.7% to 19.9% depending on the scenario, with the largest growth in shoulder months such as April, October and November because the weather becomes more favourable. The authors conclude that cycling infrastructure and services should adapt to this changing demand. Format and access: an open access journal article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY-NC-ND. Caveats: ridership models fitted on current weather responses are assumed to hold in future climates, and the counts come from one city. The framework can be used to generate climate-adjusted cycling demand for network flow and capacity planning models. It relates to the NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 climate projections and the Global High Shift Cycling Scenario in the catalogue.
